00001| #!/usr/bin/env node
00002| // Renames files by rule, not by hand (PR #1188, R1188-U5).
00003| //
00004| // The rename map, `data/meta/rename-map.lino`, holds one `rename` link per old
00005| // path and new path, each with the reason the new name says what the file
00006| // holds. This script applies the map and keeps the repository consistent:
00007| //
00008| // - It moves every renamed file, and every companion that follows from it by
00009| //   rule: the TypeScript twin (`js/x.js` -> `ts/x.ts`, `.mjs` -> `.mts`), the
00010| //   `rust/embedded/` mirror, the worker line-budget shard of a browser worker
00011| //   module (`data/meta/worker-line-budget/<stem>.lino`) and the self-AST
00012| //   census of a Rust source (`data/meta/self-ast/src/<path>.lino`) and the
00013| //   files of a Rust module's own directory (`x.rs` brings `x/child.rs`). The
00014| //   map states each rename once; the companions are not repeated in it.
00015| // - It rewrites every reference to an old path across the repository: import
00016| //   and require paths, `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` and `#[path]`
00017| //   arguments, workflow paths, seed lists, budgets, documentation links and
00018| //   test fixtures. A reference is a path token that names the old file: the
00019| //   whole path, a tail of it that no other file shares (`worker/x.js`,
00020| //   `x.js`), or a relative path that resolves to it from the referencing
00021| //   file. A token that names a different file with the same tail is left
00022| //   alone. In Rust sources it also renames the module: `mod old;` and
00023| //   `old::` paths in the same source tree.
00024| // - It re-sorts the generated one-entry-per-line lists the map names under
00025| //   `resort`, so a renamed entry lands where the list's generator puts it.
00026| //
00027| // `--check` changes nothing. It fails when an old path still exists, a new
00028| // path is missing, or any file outside the map's `exclude` prefixes still
00029| // references an old path.
00030| //
00031| // Files are moved on the filesystem by default: other agents commit from the
00032| // same working tree, and git detects the rename from the content when the move
00033| // is committed. `--git-mv` moves with `git mv` instead.
00034| //
00035| // Usage:
00036| //   node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/rename-by-rule.mjs [--tree <name>] [--dry-run] [--git-mv]
00037| //   node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/rename-by-rule.mjs --check [--tree <name>]
00038| //   node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/rename-by-rule.mjs --list [--tree <name>]

00044| const ROOT = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '../..');
00045| const MAP = 'data/meta/rename-map.lino';
00046| const LARGEST_SCANNED_FILE = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
00047| const PATH_CHARACTER = /[A-Za-z0-9_\-./~@+]/u;

00050| /** Resolve historical destination chains so later area moves preserve old rules. */
00051| export function resolveRenameChains(renames, allRenames = renames) {
00052|   const destinations = new Map(allRenames.map((rename) => [rename.from, rename.to]));
00053|   return renames.map((rename) => {
00054|     const seen = new Set([rename.from]);
00055|     let destination = rename.to;
00056|     while (destinations.has(destination)) {
00057|       if (seen.has(destination)) throw new Error(`rename cycle at ${destination}`);
00058|       seen.add(destination);
00059|       destination = destinations.get(destination);
00060|     }
00061|     if (seen.has(destination)) throw new Error(`rename cycle at ${destination}`);
00062|     return { ...rename, to: destination };
00063|   });
00064| }
00065| /**
00066|  * The directories whose Rust files are the top modules of a test binary, so
00067|  * their parent module is not written in a test path (`rust/tests/x.rs` is the
00068|  * binary `x`; `rust/tests/unit/x.rs` is `x::` in the `unit` binary).

00076| /** One indented links-notation line: its depth, head word and quoted value. */
00077| function parseLine(line) {
00078|   const depth = line.length - line.trimStart().length;
00079|   const text = line.trim();
00080|   if (text === '' || text.startsWith('#')) return null;
00081|   const space = text.indexOf(' ');
00082|   const head = space < 0 ? text : text.slice(0, space);
00083|   let value = space < 0 ? '' : text.slice(space + 1).trim();
00084|   if (value.length >= 2 && value.startsWith('"') && value.endsWith('"')) value = value.slice(1, -1).replaceAll('\\"', '"');
00085|   return { depth, head, value };

00088| /**
00089|  * The rename map: `{exclude, resort, renames}`, each rename
00090|  * `{tree, from, to, reason, review}`.
00091|  * @param {string} source
00092|  */
00093| export function parseRenameMap(source) {
00094|   const map = { exclude: [], resort: [], renames: [] };
00095|   let tree = '';
00096|   let current = null;
00097|   let renameDepth = -1;
00098|   for (const raw of source.split('\n')) {
00099|     const line = parseLine(raw);
00100|     if (!line) continue;
00101|     if (current && line.depth <= renameDepth) current = null;
00102|     if (current) {
00103|       if (['from', 'to', 'reason', 'review'].includes(line.head)) current[line.head] = line.value;
00104|       continue;
00105|     }
00106|     if (line.head === 'exclude') map.exclude.push(line.value);
00107|     else if (line.head === 'resort') map.resort.push(line.value);
00108|     else if (line.head === 'tree') tree = line.value;
00109|     else if (line.head === 'rename') {
00110|       current = { tree, from: '', to: '', reason: '', review: '' };
00111|       renameDepth = line.depth;
00112|       map.renames.push(current);
00113|     }
00114|   }
00115|   for (const rename of map.renames) {
00116|     if (!rename.from || !rename.to) throw new Error(`${MAP}: a rename in tree ${rename.tree} lacks from or to`);
00117|   }
00118|   return map;
00119| }

00121| /** Load the map and named shards without repeating shared exclusions. */
00122| export function loadRenameMap(root = ROOT) {
00123|   const visiting = new Set();
00124|   const load = (path) => {
00125|     if (visiting.has(path)) throw new Error(`rename-map include cycle at ${path}`);
00126|     visiting.add(path);
00127|     const source = readFileSync(join(root, path), 'utf8');
00128|     const map = parseRenameMap(source);
00129|     map.exclude.push(path);
00130|     for (const match of source.matchAll(/^\s*include "([^"]+)"\s*$/gmu)) {
00131|       const shard = load(match[1]);
00132|       map.exclude.push(...shard.exclude);
00133|       map.resort.push(...shard.resort);
00134|       map.renames.push(...shard.renames);
00135|     }
00136|     visiting.delete(path);
00137|     return map;
00138|   };
00139|   return load(MAP);
00140| }

00142| /** The TypeScript twin path of a `js/` source, or null. */
00143| export function typescriptTwin(path) {
00144|   if (!path.startsWith('js/')) return null;
00145|   const rest = path.slice('js/'.length);
00146|   if (rest.endsWith('.mjs')) return `ts/${rest.slice(0, -'.mjs'.length)}.mts`;
00147|   if (rest.endsWith('.jsx')) return `ts/${rest.slice(0, -'.jsx'.length)}.tsx`;
00148|   if (rest.endsWith('.js')) return `ts/${rest.slice(0, -'.js'.length)}.ts`;
00149|   return null;

00164| /**
00165|  * Every move a rename implies: the rename itself and each companion that
00166|  * exists on either side.
00167|  * @param {{from: string, to: string}} rename
00168|  * @param {(path: string) => boolean} exists

00170| export function companionMoves(rename, exists) {
00171|   const moves = [{ from: rename.from, to: rename.to, companion: '' }];
00172|   const derive = (kind, mapping) => {
00173|     for (const move of moves.slice()) {
00174|       const from = mapping(move.from);
00175|       const to = mapping(move.to);
00176|       if (from && to && from !== to && (exists(from) || exists(to))) moves.push({ from, to, companion: kind });

00178|   };
00179|   derive('typescript twin', typescriptTwin);
00180|   derive('worker line budget', workerBudgetShard);

00182|   derive('embedded mirror', (path) => `rust/embedded/${path}`);

00190| function segments(path) {
00191|   return path.split('/');

00194| /** The directory both paths share, and the rest of each below it. */
00195| export function splitCommonDirectory(from, to) {
00196|   const left = segments(from);
00197|   const right = segments(to);
00198|   let shared = 0;
00199|   while (shared < left.length - 1 && shared < right.length - 1 && left[shared] === right[shared]) shared += 1;
00200|   return { fromRest: left.slice(shared).join('/'), toRest: right.slice(shared).join('/') };

00203| /** Whether `tail` is `path` or a whole-segment tail of it. */

00208| /**
00209|  * Index tracked paths by basename, so a short reference can be told apart
00210|  * from a different file that shares its tail.
00211|  * @param {Array<string>} paths

00214|   const index = new Map();

00216|     const name = basename(path);

00223| /**
00224|  * Whether the path token `token`, written in `file`, names `target`.
00225|  * @param {string} token
00226|  * @param {string} file
00227|  * @param {string} target
00228|  * @param {Map<string, Array<string>>} byBasename
00229|  */
00230| export function tokenNames(token, file, target, byBasename) {
00231|   if (token.startsWith('./') || token.startsWith('../')) {
00232|     if (posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(file), token)) === target) return true;
00233|   }
00234|   const bare = token.replace(/^(?:\.{1,2}\/)+/u, '').replace(/^\/+/u, '');
00235|   if (bare === '') return false;
00236|   if (bare.endsWith(`/${target}`) || bare === target) return true;
00237|   if (!isSegmentTail(bare, target)) return false;
00238|   const sharing = (byBasename.get(basename(target)) ?? []).filter((path) => isSegmentTail(bare, path));
00239|   if (sharing.length <= 1) return true;
00240|   return posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(file), bare)) === target;

00243| /** The token that replaces `token` when it names `from` and `from` becomes `to`. */
00244| export function renamedToken(token, from, to) {
00245|   const { fromRest, toRest } = splitCommonDirectory(from, to);
00246|   if (token.endsWith(fromRest) && (token.length === fromRest.length || token[token.length - fromRest.length - 1] === '/')) {
00247|     return token.slice(0, token.length - fromRest.length) + toRest;
00248|   }
00249|   // A tail shorter than the part that changes: keep as many segments.
00250|   const kept = segments(token.replace(/^(?:\.{1,2}\/)+/u, '').replace(/^\/+/u, '')).length;
00251|   const lead = token.slice(0, token.length - token.replace(/^(?:\.{1,2}\/)+/u, '').replace(/^\/+/u, '').length);
00252|   const wanted = Math.max(1, kept + segments(toRest).length - segments(fromRest).length);

00256| function escapeRegExp(text) {
00257|   return text.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/gu, '\\$&');

00260| /**
00261|  * Every reference to a moved path in `text`, as `{start, end, token, move}`.
00262|  * @param {string} text
00263|  * @param {string} file
00264|  * @param {Array<{from: string, to: string}>} moves
00265|  * @param {Map<string, Array<string>>} byBasename
00266|  */
00267| export function findReferences(text, file, moves, byBasename) {
00268|   const byName = new Map();
00269|   for (const move of moves) {
00270|     const name = basename(move.from);
00271|     if (!byName.has(name)) byName.set(name, []);
00272|     byName.get(name).push(move);
00273|   }
00274|   if (byName.size === 0) return [];
00275|   const names = [...byName.keys()].sort((left, right) => right.length - left.length);
00276|   const pattern = new RegExp(names.map(escapeRegExp).join('|'), 'gu');
00277|   const found = [];
00278|   for (const match of text.matchAll(pattern)) {
00279|     const end = match.index + match[0].length;
00280|     const after = text[end] ?? '';
00281|     if (WORD_CHARACTER.test(after) || after === '-' || (after === '.' && WORD_CHARACTER.test(text[end + 1] ?? ''))) continue;

00283|     if (start > 0 && text[start - 1] !== '/' && PATH_CHARACTER.test(text[start - 1])) continue;

00286|     const move = byName.get(match[0]).find((candidate) => tokenNames(token, file, candidate.from, byBasename));
00287|     if (move) found.push({ start, end, token, move });

00292| /** The Rust module name a `.rs` path declares, or null. */
00293| function rustModuleName(path) {
00294|   if (!path.endsWith('.rs')) return null;
00295|   const name = basename(path, '.rs');
00296|   return ['mod', 'main', 'lib'].includes(name) ? basename(dirname(path)) : name;

00299| /** The source tree a Rust file belongs to (`rust/src`, `rust/tests`, ...). */
00300| function rustTree(path) {
00301|   return segments(path).slice(0, 2).join('/');
00302| }

00304| /** Whether `file` is the Rust file that declares the modules of `directory`. */
00305| function declaresModulesOf(file, directory) {
00306|   if (file === `${directory}.rs`) return true;
00307|   return posix.dirname(file) === directory && ['mod.rs', 'main.rs', 'lib.rs'].includes(basename(file));

00310| /** The module name of the directory that holds a Rust file (`ci-cd` -> `ci_cd`). */
00311| function parentModuleName(path) {

00315| /**
00316|  * Every `old::` module path that names a renamed Rust module, in any file:
00317|  * a test filter or a test name such as `ci_cd::old::case` in a durations list,
00318|  * a workflow or a document. An occurrence names the move when the module name
00319|  * is unique among the Rust files of the repository, or, among namesakes, when
00320|  * it is qualified by the parent module (`ci_cd::old::`) or, unqualified, when
00321|  * exactly one namesake sits at the root of a test binary (its parent module is
00322|  * not written in test paths). Inside a Rust source of the same source tree an
00323|  * unqualified occurrence follows the source's own rule instead (see
00324|  * `renameRustModules`).
00325|  * @param {string} text
00326|  * @param {string} file
00327|  * @param {Array<{from: string, to: string}>} moves
00328|  * @param {Map<string, Array<string>>} byBasename
00329|  * @returns {Array<{start: number, end: number, from: string, to: string, move: object}>}
00330|  */
00331| export function findModuleReferences(text, file, moves, byBasename) {
00332|   const found = [];
00333|   for (const move of moves) {
00334|     const oldName = rustModuleName(move.from);
00335|     const newName = rustModuleName(move.to);
00336|     if (!oldName || !newName || oldName === newName) continue;

00354| /**

00429| /** Sort each run of one-entry-per-line quoted list items, as their generators do. */
00430| export function resortQuotedLists(text) {
00431|   const lines = text.split('\n');
00432|   const item = /^\s*"[^"]*",\s*$/u;
00433|   for (let start = 0; start < lines.length; start += 1) {
00434|     if (!item.test(lines[start])) continue;

00436|     while (end < lines.length && item.test(lines[end])) end += 1;
00437|     const sorted = lines.slice(start, end).sort((left, right) => (left < right ? -1 : left > right ? 1 : 0));
00438|     lines.splice(start, end - start, ...sorted);
00439|     start = end;
00440|   }
00441|   return lines.join('\n');
